newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Oct 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Oct 15.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Nine people, mostly civilians, were killed and 17 were injured when soldiers and Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) rebels renewed bloody clashes on Saturday around a controversial government dam project site in north Cotabato, military and MILF sources said on Monday. (MANILA STANDARD)
- Laban party co-founder Senator Neptali Gonzalez resigned from the party on Monday saying it was "no longer the same party I helped found." (TODAY)

- Governor Nur Misuari of the Autonomous Region for Moslem Mindanao is having a hard time selecting members of his cabinet because of the short tenure of office and the image of corruption surrounding the local government. (MALAYA)
- The mysterious poison which killed up to 30,000 kilos of fish in Manila Bay had dissipated but authorities were yet to identify the culprit who dumped it there. (THE PHILIPPINE STAR)

- The Energy Regulatory Board is expected to announce shortly a wave of price increases in oil products such as diesel and liquified petroleum gas - two items used by a large segment of the population. (THE MANILA TIMES)

- Petrochemicals Corp of Asia Pacific is leading a corporate uprising in the ambitious naptha-cracker project, as it bats for a purely private sector initiative in the $500 million venture, booting out state-led PNOC-Petrochemical Development Corp. (THE BUSINESS DAILY)

- The Philippine Central Bank expects the peso to recover this week after it fell to a two-year low of 26.28 to the U.S. dollar as foreign exchange traders panicked following the sudden change in Senate leadership. Sergio Edeza, the central bank's director for treasury, said monetary authorities will not raise interest rates on its reverse repurchase agreements to keep the peso from further slipping. (THE MANILA TIMES)
